certification.title: Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate
Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Microsoft Fabric

content.summary: DP-700 is the exam for the Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate certification. It targets data engineers who ingest, transform, secure, monitor and optimize analytics solutions in Microsoft Fabric using SQL, PySpark and KQL. The three skill areas are weighted equally, so plan real hands-on time in a Fabric trial capacity, and give Real-Time Intelligence and KQL more attention than the official learning paths suggest.

examFormat.notes: Role-based Microsoft exams allow access to Microsoft Learn during the exam, but searching costs time. Localized versions are updated about eight weeks after the English version; you can request 30 extra minutes if the exam is not available in your language.

skillsMeasured.title: Implement and manage an analytics solution (30–35%)
subtopics: Configure Fabric workspace settings: Spark, domains, OneLake and Apache Airflow
Implement lifecycle management: version control, database projects, deployment pipelines
Configure security and governance: workspace and item access, row/column/object/folder-level security, dynamic data masking, sensitivity labels, endorsement, audit logs, OneLake security
Orchestrate processes: choose between Dataflow Gen2, pipelines and notebooks; schedules and event-based triggers; parameters and dynamic expressions

skillsMeasured.title: Ingest and transform data (30–35%)
subtopics: Design and implement full and incremental loads, dimensional model loading and streaming loading patterns
Batch: choose a data store and transformation tool, OneLake shortcuts, mirroring, pipelines, PySpark/SQL/KQL transforms, duplicates, missing and late-arriving data
Streaming: choose a streaming engine, native tables vs. shortcuts and query acceleration in Real-Time Intelligence, Eventstream, Spark structured streaming, KQL, windowing functions

skillsMeasured.title: Monitor and optimize an analytics solution (30–35%)
subtopics: Monitor ingestion, transformation and semantic model refresh; configure alerts
Identify and resolve errors in pipelines, Dataflow Gen2, notebooks, Eventhouse, Eventstream, T-SQL and OneLake shortcuts
Optimize Lakehouse tables, pipelines, warehouses, Eventstream and Eventhouse, Spark and query performance

knownGaps.title: KQL and Real-Time Intelligence are deeper than the learning path
knownGaps.detail: Several candidates report multiple questions that require reading or completing KQL queries (summarize, bin, windowing, materialized views, update policies) and choosing between Eventhouse native tables, shortcuts and query acceleration. The official path only introduces KQL basics.
knownGaps.recommendation: Work through the KQL quick reference and write windowing and aggregation queries against a sample Eventhouse until you can read them without running them.

knownGaps.title: Scenario questions on choosing Dataflow Gen2, pipeline or notebook
knownGaps.detail: Many questions describe a scenario (skills of the team, volume, low-code requirement, need for PySpark) and ask which tool to use. The modules teach each tool separately but not the trade-offs.
knownGaps.recommendation: Build a one-page decision table for Dataflow Gen2, pipelines, notebooks, KQL and T-SQL with their strengths, and test it against the practice assessment.

knownGaps.title: Granular security: OneLake security, RLS, CLS, OLS and masking
knownGaps.detail: Candidates mention detailed questions on which permission level or security feature applies where (workspace roles vs. item permissions vs. OneLake security vs. SQL endpoint security), and dynamic data masking syntax.
knownGaps.recommendation: Practise each security layer in a trial workspace and read the OneLake security overview end to end.

knownGaps.title: Hands-on lifecycle management: Git integration and deployment pipelines
knownGaps.detail: Questions on deployment rules, branching with Git integration and database projects assume hands-on experience. The learning path covers them briefly and without exercises for every item type.
knownGaps.recommendation: Connect a trial workspace to a Git repository, create a three-stage deployment pipeline, and deploy a lakehouse, notebook and warehouse with deployment rules.

knownGaps.title: Troubleshooting errors across items
knownGaps.detail: The monitor-and-optimize area includes resolving errors in pipelines, Dataflow Gen2, notebooks, Eventstream and shortcuts. Candidates say these questions rely on knowing the Monitoring hub and typical error messages, which the modules barely show.
knownGaps.recommendation: Deliberately break a pipeline, a notebook and a shortcut in your trial workspace and fix them using the Monitoring hub and item run history.

checklist.title: Read the official DP-700 study guide
checklist.detail: Read the skills measured as of October 19, 2026 and the change log. Mark each bullet as known, partly known or new.

checklist.title: Take the free practice assessment as a baseline
checklist.detail: Do it cold, before studying, and note the weakest skill area.

checklist.title: Start a Fabric trial capacity
checklist.detail: Activate the 60-day trial and create a dedicated study workspace. Time your study so the trial covers your exam date.

checklist.title: Book the exam for a date 6 to 8 weeks out
checklist.detail: A fixed date keeps the plan honest. Choose online proctored or a test center.

checklist.title: Complete the Ingest data with Microsoft Fabric path
checklist.detail: Do every exercise in your trial workspace, not just the reading.

checklist.title: Complete the Implement a Lakehouse path
checklist.detail: Focus on Delta tables, incremental loads, medallion layers and table maintenance (OPTIMIZE, V-Order, VACUUM).

checklist.title: Complete the Real-Time Intelligence path
checklist.detail: Build an Eventstream into an Eventhouse and query it with KQL.

checklist.title: Go deeper on KQL than the learning path
checklist.detail: Practise summarize, bin, make-series, joins, windowing and update policies. This is the most cited gap in pass reports.

checklist.title: Complete the data warehouse path
checklist.detail: Load with T-SQL and COPY INTO, then practise warehouse security and query performance.

checklist.title: Practise every security layer hands-on
checklist.detail: Configure workspace roles, item permissions, OneLake security, RLS, CLS, OLS and dynamic data masking on the same data.

checklist.title: Set up Git integration and a deployment pipeline
checklist.detail: Connect the workspace to Git and deploy items across three stages with deployment rules.

checklist.title: Write a decision table for Dataflow Gen2, pipeline and notebook
checklist.detail: One page that says when each tool (and KQL or T-SQL) is the right choice. Check it against the decision guide.

checklist.title: Break and fix a pipeline, a notebook and a shortcut
checklist.detail: Diagnose each failure from the Monitoring hub and run history, as the troubleshooting questions expect.

checklist.title: Work through one full community video course
checklist.detail: Pick one series and follow along in your workspace rather than watching passively.

checklist.title: Score 80% or more on the practice assessment twice
checklist.detail: Read the explanation for every miss and follow the linked docs.

checklist.title: Review the known gaps in this brief
checklist.detail: Revisit KQL, tool choice, security layers, lifecycle management and troubleshooting one final time.

checklist.title: Try the exam sandbox and plan your time
checklist.detail: Practise the case study layout and decide how much time to reserve for it. Use Microsoft Learn during the exam only for quick lookups.

checklist.title: Run the online proctoring system test the day before
checklist.detail: Check your webcam, network and a clear desk; have ID ready 30 minutes before the appointment.

warnings: The skills outline changed on 2026-10-19 (minor changes to workspace settings and performance optimization). Some third-party courses may predate it.
Exam price varies by country; check the exam page for your region.
